title: Congress of Vienna
summary: Representatives from some 200 European states and political entities met in Vienna from September 1814 to June 1815, after decades of war that began with the French Revolution and the Napoleonic Wars. Harvard Gazette reports that they meant to avoid future war by setting up the Congress System of periodic diplomatic conferences. Brown University Library notes the borders they set served to maintain the balance of power, and that nationalists were not always happy with them.

importance.justification: Reorganized post-Napoleonic European borders and established the Concert of Europe diplomatic framework, maintaining continent-wide stability for nearly a century.

related.because: The collapse and military defeat of Napoleon's First French Empire necessitated the diplomatic renegotiation of European borders at Vienna.

beats.caption: Diplomats from Austria, Britain, Prussia, Russia, and France assemble in Vienna to restructure post-Napoleonic Europe.
The Final Act establishes the Congress System, averting general European war for nearly a century until 1914.
